title: Contrepreneurs: The Mikkelsen Twins
summary: Debunker dissects a done-for-you audiobook course and tests the method by commissioning and writing books, finding content-mill economics, ToS violations and near-zero sales.

assertions.quote: Advice costs very little to manufacture, requires no raw materials, weighs nothing, and is evaluated in hindsight.

verdicts.note: Information goods have near-zero marginal cost and are credence goods, which economics identifies as a setting ripe for overpricing.

assertions.quote: the presentation itself is, of course, pre-recorded and slots are available 24 hours a day

verdicts.note: Evergreen webinar software and false-urgency timers are standard in online course funnels and have featured in regulator complaints.

assertions.quote: In the months that A Skeptics Guide to Hypnosis has been available, it has sold... one copy.

verdicts.note: Self-publishing platform data show most titles sell very few copies, though a minority of keyword-targeted books do earn steady royalties.

assertions.quote: the only way the economics work out is if you can under-pay your writer 90%

verdicts.note: At professional ghostwriting rates a short nonfiction book costs thousands, far above the expected royalties of a keyword-targeted title.

assertions.quote: a lot of what they’re telling you to do is actually violating the terms of service for the platforms that you’re using

verdicts.note: Major retailers prohibit reciprocal and incentivized reviews and have removed reviews and banned accounts for it.

assertions.quote: they’re selling you a method that they’ve already used up

verdicts.note: A widely documented pattern across dropshipping, FBA and publishing gurus, though not every seller has abandoned the underlying business.

assertions.quote: there was a narrow window of time where Audible’s gates were wide open, but there wasn’t a lot of competition yet

verdicts.note: Easily replicated strategies see returns compete away as entrants flood in, consistent with observed cycles in self-publishing and dropshipping niches.

assertions.quote: framing any failure as your fault rather than a flaw in the system itself

verdicts.note: A characterization of rhetorical strategy rather than a measurable outcome.

assertions.quote: your success can be, and most likely will be, zero

verdicts.note: Regulator cases and income disclosures for business-opportunity programs show most buyers earn little or nothing, though data specific to publishing courses is thin.

assertions.quote: while their success, and the success of all the testimonials they include, is exceptional, your success will probably be proportional

verdicts.note: Automators' own fine print concedes the founder's results are not typical because he is an experienced ecommerce seller and that it does not track customers' typical results; the FTC says its testimonials are atypical and most clients lose.

assertions.quote: They say it’s worth tens of thousands, with numbers they pulled right out of their ass

verdicts.note: Value stacking with arbitrary dollar figures is a standard course-funnel tactic with no independent basis for the stated values.

assertions.quote: if your card gets declined, which is completely normal, try again or just give a quick call to your bank

verdicts.note: Consumer complaints and regulator actions against coaching programs repeatedly cite pressure to finance fees with credit.

assertions.quote: the highest performers get recruited as "coaches"

verdicts.note: Coach-recruitment tiers are common in coaching programs, but they lack the multi-level commission structure that defines an MLM.
